title: The Surface Laptop Ultra delivers on most of Microsoft's promises
gist: Ars finds the $2,599-$5,899 Surface Laptop Ultra, built on Nvidia's ARM-based RTX Spark N1X, delivers strong hardware, AAA gaming and a 70B-parameter local LLM, but Copilot+ features, AI tooling, drivers and encode support lag until late 2026 or early 2027. The review frames RTX Spark PCs as rushed to market for the 2026 holiday season in a shrinking PC market.

insights.claim: Microsoft is aiming the Surface Laptop Ultra at the MacBook Pro buyer, betting people will pay a premium for one machine that does both gaming and development rather than owning a gaming desktop and a work laptop.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Tests whether a converged ARM/Blackwell device can take share in high-end laptops from Apple.
insights.locator: Microsoft is throwing both arms around

insights.claim: Total PC shipments fell 20 percent year over year in the third quarter of 2026 across the board, driven by the 'RAMpocalypse' that has exploded consumer prices and an industry fixated on enterprise money.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Memory-driven price inflation is suppressing unit demand; read-through to PC OEMs and component makers.
insights.locator: The Surface Laptop Ultra arrives at a strange time

insights.claim: Dell's XPS 16 Creator Edition and Asus's ProArt series also use the RTX Spark chipset, indicating a broader OEM wave around the Nvidia ARM platform.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Nvidia is extending into Windows PCs via multiple OEMs; watch adoption across vendors.
insights.locator: Microsoft isn’t the only one debuting

insights.claim: Pricing runs from $2,599.99 for a 24GB base model on Windows 11 Home to $5,899 at the top, with the 64GB reviewed unit at $4,299.99, and the reviewer sees 64GB as the sweet spot while questioning whether 24GB suffices.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Premium pricing narrows the buyer pool to developers and enthusiasts.

insights.claim: The RTX Spark N1X pairs a Grace CPU with a Blackwell GPU, has no dedicated NPU, and leans on unified memory and the GPU for AI work, yet Microsoft is extending the Copilot+ label despite its traditional 40+ TOPS NPU requirement.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Nvidia's GPU-centric design challenges the NPU-based Copilot+ model used by Intel, AMD and Qualcomm.
insights.locator: According to Nvidia, the RTX Spark N1X

insights.claim: Unified memory lets the system allocate 46.7GiB of its 64GiB as VRAM for a game, enabling workloads that discrete laptop GPUs cannot handle.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Large unified memory pool is the key differentiator for local AI and gaming on this platform.

insights.claim: Llama3.3-70b (43GB) ran GPU-only at 6.26 tokens per second through Ollama, a model unlikely to run on any discrete laptop GPU, though fans ran at 100 percent.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Evidence that unified-memory ARM laptops can host 70B-class models locally, a selling point for local-AI developers.

insights.claim: Mistral 7B Instruct 0.2 ran CPU-only at about 11 tokens per second in AI Dev Gallery, and Stable Diffusion v1.4 generated images in three to four seconds on the GPU via NvTensorRT.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Small models are comfortable on CPU alone; GPU paths are fast where they exist.

insights.claim: The AI software stack is immature: all conversational Phi and Mistral models in AI Dev Gallery are CPU-only, the app crashed twice, a CUDA Phi setup failed on a missing ARM64-compatible onnxruntime-gpu, and Geekbench AI offered only the CPU path.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: ARM64 CUDA tooling gaps limit near-term developer value; watch for packaging fixes.
insights.locator: On paper, AI Dev Gallery should have been

insights.claim: Phi Silica, Microsoft's flagship on-device LLM, is gated behind developer registration with an app identity, so it is not ready-to-run out of the box.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Friction undermines the advertised out-of-box Copilot+ experience.
insights.locator: Phi Silica, Microsoft’s flagship on-device LLM

insights.claim: Microsoft said full Copilot+ software support won't arrive until late 2026 or early 2027, so Recall, Click to Do and the new Windows search bar are unavailable, and the Copilot key currently launches cloud M365 Copilot.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Launch-to-feature gap lowers near-term value; monitor Windows Insider releases for timing.
insights.quote: “full software support won’t arrive until late 2026 or early 2027.”
insights.locator: According to Microsoft in the review information session

insights.claim: Nvidia NVENC and HEVC encode options are missing in HandBrake, so the Blackwell encode engine isn't exposed, and the CPU x264 encode of a 10-minute 4K60 clip took 2:27 at 180 fps.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Driver exposure gaps limit creator workflows until Nvidia and Microsoft ship updates.

insights.claim: The reviewer concludes PCs are being rushed to market on RTX Spark so manufacturers have something new for the 2026 holiday season, with software left to catch up on a non-specific date.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Early buyers are beta testers; wait for software maturity before purchases or channel-check strength.
insights.quote: The problem isn’t the laptop’s hardware, but everything currently sitting on top of it.

insights.claim: Gears of War: E-Day and Forza Horizon 6 ran well on the ARM machine with full DLSS and ray tracing options, and Microsoft claims 85 percent of the Game Pass library is playable on ARM, though kernel-level anti-cheat such as Easy Anti-Cheat may flag Prism emulation.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: ARM gaming viability is improving; anti-cheat compatibility remains the main gating risk.

insights.claim: The laptop retained 66 percent battery after three hours of varied use, with a significant drop when running llama3.3:70b twice.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Heavy local AI burns battery quickly, limiting the all-day single-device pitch.
